## Figure caption (auxiliary; use the image as primary evidence)

The image contains three subfigures, labeled (a), (b), and (c). Each subfigure illustrates different atomic orbitals with respect to the nucleus, shown as a red dot.

(a) Shows a spherical distribution of dots around the nucleus, indicating the \(n=2\), \(\ell=0\), \(m_\ell=0\) orbital. The dots are concentrated in a circular shell around the nucleus.

(b) Depicts a two-lobed shape along the z-axis, representing the \(n=2\), \(\ell=1\), \(m_\ell=0\) orbital. The lobes are symmetrically placed above and below the nucleus. The axes \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) are labeled.

(c) Illustrates a donut-shaped distribution in the x-y plane, corresponding to the \(n=2\), \(\ell=1\), \(m_\ell=\pm1\) orbital. The axes \(x\), \(y\), and \(z\) are labeled, with the nucleus at the center.

Each subfigure includes a label for the nucleus and annotations describing the quantum numbers.
